narrative.overview: A video travels from its own language to Uzbek the way a train runs a metro line: Havola, Nutq, Tarjima, Ovoz, Tayyor. Marble walls (light) or night-station granite (dark), enamel plaques with a thick base rule, round station markers on one continuous line, and line colours that mean something. Proof is concrete: the real form is the ticket machine, numbers sit on a dated station board, the train stops at the job's real stage.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous red spine with ring stops
Granite plaques with line-colour base rules
Semantic line colours, one active at a time
Flat surfaces, 6px plates, brass hairline frames

rules.name: The One Active Line Rule
rules.body: At most one line colour is filled at a time; other services show a coloured dot on ink/ghost controls.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Rule
rules.body: Red, blue and green never decorate; generic actions are ink.

rules.name: The Signage Rule
rules.body: Condensed caps for names and headings only; never body sentences.

rules.name: The Flat Wall Rule
rules.body: No glass, blur or glow; depth comes from material.

dos: Do put long pages on the Spine
Do use *-ink variants for coloured text (>=4.5:1)
Do date every statistic and source it from production
Do keep the URL field and start button in the first viewport
donts: Don't fill more than one line colour at a time
Don't use gradients, glass, blur or glows
Don't put eyebrow labels above headings
Don't use brass as text or add a second typeface
Don't interrupt the first viewport with a modal
